memory_holds.py::pending_removals.ends: PREPCLEAN-4 (decision 309): a successor reads at most MAX_PENDING_REMOVALS (64, the run-slot diagnostic bound) recorded folder removals of other instances per read. A record ends when the folder is observed absent (removal_proven rewrites it as removed with no folder), after which it is no longer read; a full read is repeated once every record of it is done. The record lives in the preparation row's evidence, which stays as that row's tombstone, so no new table or hold kind exists.

memory_holds.py::_read_pending.ends: HM2A-11: the same pending read as pending_workspaces, per project: it stops reading rows past MAX_PENDING_REMOVALS (64) and the caller answers unknown (None); nothing is stored between passes, each pass reads afresh under one deadline.

memory_holds.py::pending_workspaces_deta.ends: HM-2a wiring (S11): one health pass reads at most MAX_PENDING_READ_PROJECTS (256) project folders and at most MAX_PENDING_REMOVALS (64) pending removal records per project, through the primary-key range of that project's preparation rows (no full-table scan, no temporary sort), under one monotonic deadline (PENDING_DEADLINE_SECONDS, 2 s, checked by a SQLite progress handler cleared in finally and in each Python loop); nothing is kept between passes, and a read that meets a bound or the deadline answers unknown (None), never a partial set, so the workspaces check removes nothing that pass and says so. No state, count or record is stored; each pass reads afresh.

project_driver.py::_step_removals.ends: PREPCLEAN-4 (decision 309): at most MAX_PENDING_REMOVALS inherited removals are in memory (the read bound); each keeps only its folder, capped pause and deadline (the sixty-second cap of cleanup retries, no attempt count) and ends when the folder is observed absent and its proof recorded. The read is asked again only after a full one is all done.

orchestration_api.py::checked_resume_sta.ends: U1: per-checkpoint canonical JSON size (2048 bytes), replaced by the next recorded state and removed with closed orchestration retention; no cumulative count.

orchestration_lifetime.py::_capacity_due.ends: U1: registration attempt rows, open report rows, mixed distinct report runs and journal events belong to one orchestration. At each safe-point continuation the product atomically closes it and opens a successor before admitting more work; the old report and replay remain available during existing retention.

health_holds.py::execute.ends: HM-3 observation pages only, never admission limits. Each statement seeks its last key through an existing index, and exhaustion wraps. Deleted sources leave the set; later pages remain reachable. No retained-history count can refuse work.

health_holds.py::check_account.ends: HM-3 observation pages only, never admission limits. Each statement seeks its last key through an existing index, and exhaustion wraps. Deleted sources leave the set; later pages remain reachable. No retained-history count can refuse work.

health_holds.py::projects_page.ends: HM-3 observation pages only, never admission limits. Each statement seeks its last key through an existing index, and exhaustion wraps. Deleted sources leave the set; later pages remain reachable. No retained-history count can refuse work.

health_holds.py::_legacy_deadline.ends: Consistency precondition: at most two indexed legacy intents decide ambiguity; no lifetime/admission population ceiling. Two matching retained intents prove ambiguity, so later matches cannot change the answer. The existing records_run index seeks the run, and the two-row evidence window is rebuilt for each check. Three matching rows still yield ambiguous, and removing two restores the single-intent answer.

health_workspaces.py::_pass.ends: HM-2a: MAX_REMOVALS_PER_PASS counts removals in one pass only (it starts again at 0 every pass; the folders left over are reported as waiting and removed at the next pass, and a folder that is removed leaves the listing); PENDING_REPORT_PASSES is a number of passes a folder is pending, kept only for folders pending now and dropped when the driver removes the folder; MIN_ORPHAN_AGE_SECONDS (twice) is an age, not a count, and never alone allows a removal (the owner's free lock does)

health_workspaces.py::read.ends: HM-2a: MAX_ENTRIES_SCANNED (entries of the projects folder), MAX_JOURNAL_PROJECTS, MAX_JOURNAL_NAMES (names in launch folders) and MAX_JOURNAL_ENTRIES bound one read of the launch journals, each counted while listing; past any of them the live set is reported as incomplete and nothing is removed that pass; journals are pruned by the driver (settled entries end after their tombstone time) and the count is taken afresh at every pass

health_workspaces.py::_listing.ends: HM-2a: MAX_ENTRIES_SCANNED and MAX_FOLDERS_LISTED bound what one pass reads of the scratch container: every entry read counts, and the time share is checked every _LISTING_DEADLINE_EVERY entries; the listing a pass stopped in is kept (one open listing of the pinned container, closed when it ends, when the container at that path is another folder, on an error, or by close()) and the next pass goes on with it, so entries past the cap are reached at later passes and a pass never reads more than the cap

health_workspaces.py::_records.ends: HM-2a: MAX_RECORD_ITEMS (items, repeats included) and MAX_RECORD_PATHS (distinct paths, counted after deduplication) bound what a record reader may hand back in one pass; past either the set is incomplete, nothing is removed and the pass says so; nothing is stored between passes

health_workspaces.py::spent.ends: HM-2a: MAX_REMOVAL_ENTRIES_PER_PASS counts entries removed in one pass only (a new budget every pass); a folder not finished keeps its owner marker (removed last) and its removal goes on at the next pass

health_workspaces.py::_remove_tree.ends: HM-2a: MAX_REMOVAL_DEPTH bounds how deep the descriptor remover goes (one descriptor per level); a folder deeper than that is reported as not removed at every pass and left for a person (it keeps its marker); nothing is counted across passes

health_workspaces.py::_owner.ends: HM-2a: MAX_MARKER_BYTES is a size check on one owner marker read (not a count); a larger file is not a marker, so its folder is only reported

health_workspaces.py::_finish.ends: HM-2a: MAX_MARKER_BYTES is a size check on the owner marker read once more just before it is removed (to put it back if the folder's rmdir fails); not a count, nothing is kept

account_billing_jobs.py::_settle_ended.ends: S12 N3: three non-transient record failures per unknown job, then denial; busy SQL never consumes the budget. Failed denial retries without repeating exhausted record attempts. Settled jobs never retry. The counter ends with the job at account replacement.

health_ledger.py::_load.ends: Per-store health metadata reads at most 1024 bytes plus the excess-byte probe; invalid metadata is reported and a new full check is scheduled. Observations and saved state for removed projects are pruned after a bounded registry scan.

health_ledger.py::measure.ends: Report-only size/rate limits. Growth requires six hours; daily renewal keeps the older sample until its replacement matures, then discards it. Truncation or backward clock correction resets both samples; eviction/project pruning drops candidates. No admission or record is refused.

health_ledger.py::completion_findings.ends: The 24-hour completion clock raises a warning only. Completing the full copy check clears overdue; starting or pausing never does.

health_ledger.py::visit.ends: A full copy is scheduled before the daily deadline; one active copy continues across slices until complete. No project is excluded by database size or age.

health_ledger.py::step.ends: Deadline of one granted copy slice. COPY_PAGES is owned by the backup runner, not step; new expired-deadline row checks no grant. Each grant advances eight pages of the same Python backup VM, on one exclusive snapshot worker. Its read transaction pins the WAL snapshot across passes; WAL writers keep committing.

health_ledger.py::_progress.ends: Progress callbacks yield while their granted deadline is expired. Count increment is bookkeeping, not a count cap. Backup and quick/full copy VMs pause between grants. One copy worker and one scan worker per check; cleanup joins before deletion and gates the next job.

health_ledger.py::_copy_slice.ends: Shared copy deadline, shortened under queue pressure to BUSY_COPY_SECONDS; inherited stub consumes time past that slice. A shared owner deadline bounds copying; a pending foreground queue reduces the copy quantum to 150 ms. Work resumes in later passes and uses spare time when idle.

health_ledger.py::_retain.ends: The 32-store in-memory cache evicts old observations to bounded per-store metadata. Status loads the requested project independently, and registry traversal continues past the cache ceiling. Project metadata lives with that project and is deleted with it.

health_ledger.py::_select.ends: Read-only indexed next-project lookup LIMIT 1 with a cursor; no project admission ceiling. One indexed project identity per pass, using a keyset cursor; registry exhaustion restarts the scan. Projects beyond the page are checked on later passes.

user_settings.py::load.ends: Read at most 4096 bytes plus one probe. Validate typed bounds with whole-file default fallback and plain warnings; no persisted records or users are capped. S9/S10/S35 share this loader.

run_retention.py::page.ends: An indexed maintenance page of at most 32 records. The cursor advances even over protected rows; records end in immutable summaries. No admission cap.

run_retention.py::sweep.ends: Scalar batch validation; actual bounded SQL work is independently registered as nested page. One page at most 32 records; only maintenance, resumes after the page and skips readers/transactions. Not a run admission cap. SQL selection is limited to 2048 callbacks and 25 ms.

learning_contracts.py::validate_retentio.ends: Stored summaries have at most 32 represented records, the maintenance page bound. This is a record shape bound, never admission or accumulated history. Keep the stored-reader bound even if the live page shrinks.

learning_store.py::_retention_detail.ends: Read-only indexed membership lookup; bounded query is nested read, no outer historical population ceiling remains. Historical lookup seeks one proven, typed summary member under the existing 2048-callback/25-ms read budget. Missing IDs stay not found; a budget refusal propagates without inventing membership. The connection-local index rebuilds from permanent summaries.

run_retention.py::advance_import_history.ends: Imported summaries are rebuilt into the connection-local lookup in pages of at most 32 on project-owner maintenance; the page cursor advances and then drops, so it is neither an admission cap nor accumulated history. Summaries stay permanent history.

run_retention.py::rows.ends: The ledger's lookup rebuild reads at most 32 permanent summaries per owner turn and resumes from its committed cursor; the cursor ends at the last summary. A page bound, never an admission cap.

run_retention.py::_component.ends: The bounded recursive page ends at batch+1; oversized linked groups stay full and later candidates advance. No admission capacity limit.

runtime_lineage.py::release_versions.ends: One bounded read of the shipped catalogue; excess bytes refuse trust and retain custody.

runtime_lineage.py::successor_custody.ends: At most 16 immutable lineage links per verification, not a lifetime record cap; longer or cyclic paths keep custody.

takeover_journal.py::validate.ends: A1: fixed integer, version, path, authorization and at-most-64 listed-run widths; one journal ends at completion or pre-stop undo.

takeover_journal.py::read.ends: One journal is at most 16 KiB, removed after completion or pre-stop undo; an oversized file is retained and refused.

takeover_journal.py::write.ends: Bounded intent bytes, not a lifetime run count; no replacement is made when it cannot fit.

takeover_journal.py::create.ends: Prior authorization cannot exceed 1 KiB; refused before intent and any stop.

takeover_process.py::identity.ends: One kernel argument read is bounded to 4 MiB; uninspectable or oversized arguments never authorize a signal.

update_takeover.py::stop_until_excluded.ends: At most three stop/probe rounds after the start barrier; an inherited lock leaves a resumable failure, never adoption.

update_takeover.py::run.ends: Phase-index comparisons only, not admission counts; the finite intent is removed on completion or pre-stop undo.

update_takeover.py::installed.ends: Phase ordering only; the installed phase cannot precede account completion.

update_takeover.py::complete.ends: Phase ordering only; successful completion removes the journal.

takeover_owner.py::stop_collector.ends: A finite protocol-version split and one 30-second authenticated collector stop, never a lifetime count; an exceeded stop budget remains resumable.

takeover_preflight.py::_registry.ends: Read-only registry/status aggregation COUNT and schema-version compatibility; never compares a child population with a ceiling. The old CLI-message-only binding was wrong. COUNT(*) is a read-only diagnostic of live, unreleased child slots. It imposes no limit and refuses no update; normal authenticated settlement or crash grace ends each slot.

takeover_preflight.py::read_plan.ends: Five seconds for a starting service to publish a hint or release history/host flocks; absent service then project_store_busy. Authorization read remains capped at 1 KiB.

account_takeover.py::takeover_report.ends: At most eight rows and 14 KiB per read-only diagnostic page, with a continuation offset. More projects/bytes continue on the next page, never refuse a run or release any custody. COUNT(*) supplies diagnostic totals only.

takeover_process.py::_darwin_argv.ends: One kernel-declared argument buffer, capped at 4 MiB before allocation or reading. Excess or an unreadable kernel limit refuses proof without a signal.

takeover_journal.py::reconcile.ends: Mixed site: 1070 launch rows are bounded to MAX_TAKEOVER_RUNS=64; classify demonstrated run count rather than bytes. Complete widest serialized journal <=16384 bytes; excess unsettled runs are counted durably, never dropped from totals.

takeover_journal.py::widest.ends: Conservative widest-document construction is a serialization precondition used by reconcile; widest itself has no quota comparison or retained population. Reserves all future fields at 2^63-1 before selecting runs; at most 64 copied rows per takeover.

takeover_owner.py::stop_service.ends: Unproven hint: 30-second stop wait, never a signal. Proven idle candidate first gets that withdrawal opportunity; if still live it uses the same 30-second TERM plus 5-second KILL pin as a busy predecessor. New stop-op services have one 30-second lock/ack wait. Held locks always prevent adoption.

takeover_process.py::stop.ends: One TERM, 30 seconds; then same pinned target KILL, five seconds. No signal without last identity check.

takeover_owner.py::withdraw_hint.ends: hint.lock is held briefly by a service; after five seconds return service_stop_failed, preserving resumable intent.

takeover_owner.py::run_owner_takeover.ends: collector-runtime.lock wait ends at 20 seconds with write-free update_busy. Descriptor is retained through owner restart.

client_runtime.py::account_takeover_repo.ends: At most ceil(64/PAGE_SIZE)+1 pages; offsets must strictly increase; failure returns no diagnostic.

project_takeover.py::purge_takeover.ends: takeover_runs drain with attempt replay retention (<=64 per update); orphan run rows expire by recorded_at_ms. Obligations end with hold/settlement evidence. Newest record and references stay, every complete unreferenced record except the newest 16 is removed in one separate atomic pass.

runtime_lineage.py::lineage_status.ends: Over64 is diagnostic only, never update refusal or protected-row eviction.

takeover_process.py::wait.ends: Both birth fallback and kqueue waits end at their passed deadline (30 seconds TERM / 5 seconds KILL). NOTE_EXEC is retained for I4 and never mistaken for exit or timeout.

takeover_owner.py::_service_answers.ends: A single scope-endpoint connect waits at most 0.2 seconds. An unreadable or timed-out endpoint remains live; only ENOENT/ECONNREFUSED proves it no longer answers. The enclosing stop deadline ends the loop.

runtime_lineage.py::_scan.ends: S14F-1/-5: a per-pass work budget (CUSTODY_PASS_ROWS units: lineage edges read by key page with LIMIT ?, then rowid windows of already-retained history counted with COUNT), not an admission or lifetime cap. The cycle state is in memory on the store and ends when the cycle completes, its clock goes before the cycle start (S14F-4), the change watch, another connection's commit or a schema change/VACUUM invalidates it (S14F-6), or the store closes; the rows it reads are removed by their own retention. Nothing is refused by it; an unfinished pass resumes on the next sweep.

runtime_lineage.py::_drain.ends: S14F-9: a reset hands the old cycle's containers (edges, order, custody set, protected set) to the drop list in O(1); each later pass empties at most its remaining budget of items from them, so a 2,000-key reset spreads over passes and the list ends empty. Nothing is refused.

runtime_lineage.py::advance.ends: S14F-5: the same per-pass budget also covers the protected-path walk (consuming the custody set itself, one visited set, linear) and the paged deletions (rechecked under the write lock, S14F-8), so one owner pass does at most CUSTODY_PASS_ROWS units in total; the walk queue, visited set and deletion index end with the cycle (reset on completion or invalidation). A 2,000-edge overlapping chain past the budget completes over many passes, each within the budget, and equals the whole-scan prune.
